what_happened: The person running Athena wrote three requests in a row to stop one failing item from halting a batch drain. The first covered only paused items. The second covered only flagged items. Each time, an item that failed twice and was neither paused nor flagged stopped the batch again. The Steward had already named the general pattern, but the requests kept patching the last case seen. The person then queued the general fix: pass over any item that fails twice. This is an intervention note, not a failed job record.
cause: Athena does not list the states and routes by which one failing item can halt a drain (paused, flagged, failed twice, and others), so a request that fixes drain-stopping is written from memory of the last case seen. Nothing compares the request's scope with the code's full set of stop outcomes. Nothing warns that the scope is partial. Nothing surfaces earlier fixes for the same stop or the Steward's named pattern when a new fix is queued. Each fix is accepted as complete, and the gap shows only when the next item stops the batch by another route. Request size and coverage are not checked against the code before queueing.
prevention: Add a check at request intake for requests that fix a drain stop. It lists every outcome in the code that can halt the drain and requires the request to cover them all, or to state why an outcome is left out. It also shows the earlier fixes for the same stop and any Steward finding naming the pattern, and it flags a request narrower than the full set as partial. A test would feed a drain an item failing twice in each state (paused, flagged, neither) and assert the batch continues. That would have caught the first narrow fix and made the general fix the first request.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain continue past any single item that stops it, whatever route the item takes: paused, flagged, failed twice, failed with an environment error, or refused at commit. Outcome: after one item fails twice, the drain records it as passed over with the reason and moves to the next runnable item, and the batch does not halt while budget and slots remain. First, list in the code every state or outcome that can currently halt a drain. Acceptance: a test runs a drain over a queue where one item ends in each such state (including failed twice and neither paused nor flagged) followed by a healthy item. It asserts the healthy item runs and lands, and each passed-over item is shown in the drain summary with its reason. Passed-over items stay queued for review and are not retried in the same drain. This is one change only; do not add failure-cause grouping or other work.
